label: copy-phase input r echoed back at early copy positions (orig idx 1-3)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the fed-back input token is r, and almost only when that r is original token 1, 2 or 3 (recall_idx 2-4). It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and never on any other input token. Magnitude is largest when r is original token 1 (recall_idx 2: 41% of activations, 60% of mass; top examples are all of the form X r ... <DEL> X [r]) and falls off at later positions. An r at original position 0 (copy step L+1) gives only tiny activations, and an r at position 4 or later is essentially silent. Most false positives are r at position 3 near the end of short sequences (to_go 0-1). Dev F1 0.90, mass recall 0.999.

issues: Systematic false-positive class the explanation gets wrong: when r is fed back at the last copy step (to_go == 0), the feature is almost silent. Restricted to the predicate, (to_go == 0) gives 5578 predicted steps with precision 0.026 and mass recall 0.0003 on test. That is about 70% of the original predicate's 7915 test false positives. The explanation says the false positives are spread over to_go 0-1 and only tested to_go >= 2, which cuts recall to 0.806 and F1 to 0.874. It never tested to_go >= 1, which fixes the problem.
Adding (to_go >= 1) raises test precision from 0.830 to 0.939 while recall stays at 0.982 (it was 0.986) and mass recall stays at 0.998. Test F1 goes from 0.901 to 0.960.
The profile backs this up across the board: only 172 of 1,000,000 to_go==0 steps are active.

Claims that check out: the feature fires only in the copy phase (0 activations in the original and delimiter phases) and only on input r (100% of mass). By recall_idx, mass is 0.600 at 2, 0.338 at 3 and 0.061 at 4. recall_idx 1 is tiny (0.001) and recall_idx >= 5 is essentially zero. Precision is 0.973 at recall_idx 2, 0.850 at 3 and 0.633 at 4, so the claim that it falls off at later positions holds.

The false positives left after the to_go fix are mostly r at original position 3 (recall_idx 4) with only a few copy steps left. They make up a weaker tail and are not a new class. Misses hold 0.1% of the mass and are tiny activations on r at original position 0, which is scattered noise.
